content_of_post_to_comment: Recent study finds a meager, lousy 1% of people actually click the sources cited in AI Overviews on Google. WTF Being a former academic, this AI finding disappoints me more than many of the others I’ve seen. As an editor and someone who taught students, what drives me absolutely crazy is when people don’t cite their sources. Because you can’t verify an argument or statement if you can’t go to the original content. People hate doing it because it’s tedious, but it is absolutely essential. You also have to make sure you’re using reputable sources. Sometimes some of what these AIs draw from are personal blogs and sites that have no business being cited to begin with, which again leads me back to this: you have to check. This is exactly how rumors get started. Inaccurate findings get cited all over social media, which happens repeatedly. Data can also be interpreted in multiple ways, which makes it imperative that you read at least part of these studies to see what they’re actually saying.
comment: The deeper issue may be that citations have become a ritual rather than a habit of verification. AI could make sourcing easier, but only if users learn to treat references as starting points, not decorative footnotes.
